_comment: Structured summary of eval/BENCHMARK.md, hand-synced to the real, reproduced numbers in that file. This is the source Benchmarks.tsx/BenchmarkPage.tsx fetch via GET /benchmarks, so the live UI reads the same numbers a human reading BENCHMARK.md sees. Update this file whenever BENCHMARK.md's numbers change.
notes: The 2026-08-15 rerun (against live production, real HTTP calls) used a smaller, real 106-document local corpus and small-N per-route samples due to sandbox/network constraints — see eval/BENCHMARK.md for exact session-vs-prior sample sizes. route_comparison/stat_tiles below keep the larger-N 2026-08-10 in-process numbers (still real, more statistically meaningful) since single-digit-N reruns are noisy; both are dated in BENCHMARK.md so neither silently overwrites the other. This rerun also surfaced a real finding: this Render free-tier instance runs a single worker and degrades sharply under concurrent requests (serialized requests succeed reliably; concurrent ones time out) — see BENCHMARK.md's 'Results — rerun 2026-08-15' section.

corpus.corpus_note: 106 is what's reproducible on disk in this environment (50 CORD-v2 + 6 invoice2data + 50 FUNSD). An earlier claim of 550 documents (494 CORD-v2) needs the `datasets` package to rebuild, which this session's sandbox could not install.

robustness.note: Not re-verified at this scale 2026-08-15 — the live single-worker instance couldn't sustain concurrency 4+ for a batch this size in one session (see notes); a concurrency=1 6-doc sample that session did complete 1/6 within the time available, not a meaningful robustness measurement on its own.

route_comparison_measured: 2026-08-10, larger N (39 invoices, 40-200 receipts per route)

sroie.measured: 2026-06-19, not re-verified since (sandbox can't install the `datasets` package to pull the test split)
